caption: A curling stone glides down the ice, strikes another stone sitting in the house, and knocks it away while itself slowing to a stop.

sa.check: A curling stone glides down the ice.
It strikes another stone sitting in the house.
The struck stone is knocked away.
The striking stone slows to a stop.
The target stone is still before the contact.
The glide comes first, then the contact, then the two stones' outcomes.

pc.expect: The resting stone starts moving at the moment the gliding stone reaches it, and only then.
pc.fail: The resting stone moves before the gliding stone arrives; or the stones touch and the resting stone stays put; or the gliding stone stops short and the other moves away anyway.

pc.expect: The struck stone leaves roughly along the line of the hit while the striking stone loses most of its speed.
pc.fail: The struck stone moves off back toward the thrower; or the striking stone keeps its speed through the contact; or both stones travel on together side by side at the same speed.

pc.expect: The two stones meet at their edges and stay outside one another and on top of the ice.
pc.fail: The stones overlap or pass through each other; or one rides up over the other and keeps going; or a stone sinks into the ice.

pc.expect: On the ice each stone slides along its own line, curling only gradually and slowing steadily; a stone at rest stays at rest until it is struck.
pc.fail: A stone turns sharply on the open ice with nothing touching it; or a stone gathers speed as it slides; or a stone that has come to rest sets off again untouched.

pc.expect: The stones keep their number and shape on the sheet.
pc.fail: A stone vanishes at the contact or a third appears; or a stone's handle comes away and floats; or a stone turns into another object.

pc.expect: The stones' handles, the painted house and the ice stay the same.
pc.fail: A stone's handle changes colour at the contact; or the rings of the house shift between frames; or the markings on the sheet change.
